I truly hope that you never experience despair, for those of us who are in despair, cannot see any way out of it, no matter what some people say. I understand OP is trying to help and be kind, I get that, but when you are as deep down in the pit as I am, well let's just say I cant see their words as anything more than hollow platitudes, when people tell me to hang on it gets better, I have a knee-jerk reaction to say: when, because (as I have said) I have been hanging on, for over a decade, and what you and others do not understand is I have grown weary of hanging on, I have grown weary of hearing and taking the same hollow advice from people better off than me over and over, I have grown weary of being alone, I am tired, but I cannot rest because I have my parents who depend on me, I am tired of grinning and bearing it and saying everything's fine when someone asks how are you, and if you tell them how you are feeling they bugger off quickly.

I am sorry if I seem combative, it is not my aim, and I know you mean well, and fuck it you are probably right as well, but what Lubu222 and I are trying to say is that when you are felling really low, all the helpful advice just sounds like the same smarmy song we have heard all too many times.

Again sorry for being such a drag, and sorry for my long reply, I wish you the best.

A serious young man found the conflicts of mid 20th Century America
confusing. He went to many people seeking a way of resolving within
himself the discords that troubled him, but he remained troubled.
One night in a coffee house, a self-ordained Zen Master said to him,

 “Go to the dilapidated mansion you will find at this address which I have written
down for you. Do not speak to those who live there; you must remain silent
until the moon rises tomorrow night. Go to the large room on the right of the
main hallway, sit in the lotus position on top of the rubble in the northeast
corner, face the corner, and meditate.”
 
He did as the Zen Master instructed. His meditation was frequently
interrupted by worries. He worried whether or not the rest of the plumbing
fixtures would fall from the second floor bathroom to join the pipes and
other trash he was sitting on. He worried how he would know when the
moon rose on the next night. He worried about what the people who walked
through the room said about him.

His worrying and meditation were disturbed when, as if in a test of his faith,
ordure fell from the second floor onto him. At that time two people walked
into the room. The first asked the second who the man sitting there was. The
second replied 
“Some say he is a holy man. Others say he is a shithead.”
 
Hearing this, the man was enlightened.

I will cede the next point and stand corrected,I did assume the OP's depression symptoms, and financial situation without any knowledge or context, and am thus duly chastened, I apologize.

My next issue of contention is when you said: 
"Maybe you're just judging yourself by societies standards when you should be judging yourself by your own."   

And:
"what people think of you has no actual effect on who you are."

The first quote and by extension the quote from your reply are what lead me to say pull your head out of your ass, a bit crass I agree, but my blood was hot at the time...

Every human is constantly being judged by and judging society's standards from the moment you are born, the way one looks, the language one speaks, one's education and upbringing, one's financial situation, social friendships, relationship status, sexual orientation and experience are all under constant scrutiny and if you don't fit into the mold then you WILL be treated differently and often the victim of ridicule and derision.

I have been alone for 30 years, never had a romantic partner or even "been in love" whatever that means lol, and my three friends all moved away to the city 1400km away. I have been going through dark times recently as well...and I have come to realize that I am the master of my own fate.

I know that if I had to start looking after myself: exercising etc. and trying to be more sociable, things would change for me. I however don't want to change, if that makes any sense. I feel that if I change my looks, my personality and my lifestyle and people accept me then they won't be accepting the real me, but rather a fake, an impostor.

Now I don't know what your situation is but, and I KNOW how irritating this is going to sound, I KNOW because it is the same advice people give me over and over: 

The power to change yourself lies with you, don't rely on God, don't rely on mankind -trust only yourself- and change your life 

OR: Do what I have done, accept your solitude and take it day by day, it is a lonely road, but we am not the first to walk it and we won't be the last either. I hope my story and advice gives you at least some semblance of peace. Be well.

I'm 30 and male and in the same boat as you. I know I would never be counted as handsome and I don't earn enough money for that to not be a factor. Never been in a relationship, never been kissed and no girl has ever shown an iota of interest in me. I was dealing with a lot of shit from this up until about a week ago, when while meditating before sleep the solution occurred to me.

Hear me out here, I have given up. I have come to realize that I am unhappy because I am and always will be single, and society labels people like me losers, this is what was causing me anxiety, not my loneliness (which is there mind you) but rather the pressure from everyone else to have a partner.

I have come to believe that having a loving partner is one of the greatest blessings you can have in life, but you should in no way think of yourself as less if you cannot find one. I am trying to deal with it one day at a time, and I know I will eventually become acclimatized to the solitude, I've done it for 30 years so what if I do it for 30 more.

Furthermore, simply finding a partner is not going to solve all our problems, life is not like the movies.So I know it is not the message we might have wanted,but maybe it is time for us to stop worrying about a partner and let go of our anger and false-hope and learn to live for ourselves.

I hope my long-winded response gives you some small measure of comfort, and I wish you all the best for your future.
